card.title: How To Fix an iPhone 7 That Does Not Turn On

source.title: How To Fix an iPhone 7 That Does Not Turn On

claims.statement: iPhone 7 pulling about 2 A or more on a DC supply before power-on usually has a shorted capacitor, most often on PP_VDD_MAIN, then PP_VDD_BOOST, backlight anodes, or PP_SPKR1_VBOOST.
Inject 4 V / 2 A into the shorted line and find the cap with freeze spray or thermal camera; the shorted cap can simply be removed.

Common liquid-damage areas for a VDD_MAIN short include around BBPMU_RF (C5625_RF, C5622_RF), the back top arm (C2609–C2612), backlight caps (C3725, C3705, C4602, C4612), near WLAN (C7610_RF, C2527, C3002) and above the CPU (C3313, C3327, C3328).
When injecting through the battery connector, Tigris MOSFET Q2101 heats instantly because PP_BATT_VCC feeds VDD_MAIN through it; it is not the short.

procedure: Inspect for liquid damage (under stickers and foam).
Measure VDD_MAIN, VDD_BOOST, backlight anodes, SPKR1_VBOOST for shorts.
Inject 4 V / 2 A and locate the hot capacitor.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
